newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Hurricane Lili kills 10 in Central America.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili kills 10 in Central America.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and hundreds driven from their homes when torrential rain from Hurricane Lili lashed Central America, rescue workers and local authorities said on Thursday.
The highest death toll was in Nicaragua, where Civil Defence officials said five people had drowned in swollen rivers across the country over the past four days and 200 were left homeless.
In Costa Rica four people were killed in river tragedies and in Honduras a young toddler died when his house was washed away in a shantytown on the edge of the capital Tegucigalpa.
"Tropical Storm Lili caused extensive flooding in parts of northern Nicaragua, and five people drowned in the swollen waters," Nicaraguan Civil Defence Capt. Javier Gadea told Reuters.
Two people drowned outside the town of San Lucas in the northern department of Madriz, near the Honduran border, when they were swept away trying to cross a river swollen by Lili's rains, Gadea said.
The three drowned in the northern deparments of Esteli and Jinotega, he said.
Hundreds of people in these regions were forced to flee to high ground as swollen rivers flooded their homes and civil defence authorities were worried about the threat of mudslides, he said.
In Costa Rica, coffee officials feared damage to the country's coffee export crops after the destruction wrought by Lili.

Four people died in river tragedies as the storm lashed the Punta Arenas province, including 11-year-old Gerardo Canton Murillo, who was swept away in the river Barranca on Tuesday near Esparza, 56 miles (90 km) west of the capital San Jose.
Lili started as a tropical depression at the beginning of the week, but turned into a tropical storm on Wednesday and was upgraded to a hurricane on Wednesday night.

The weather system brushed Mexico's Yucatan coast and passed near Guatemala on its way across the Caribbean on Wednesday but both countries were spared any serious damage or loss of life, rescue officials there said.
Lili was bearing down on Cuba on Thursday, threatening the Communist-ruled island with torrential rains and flooding.
